tasks.short: Pull labour market figures, CAO wage updates and agency rate data into one sheet for HR and finance.

today.trigger: Monthly HR review, a vacancy that stays open, or a director's question about wages or flex costs.
steps: Download CBS StatLine and UWV regional vacancy figures for Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo
Check CAO Beroepsgoederenvervoer and warehouse CAO wage table updates
Copy hours and rates from the three staffing agency portals
Paste everything into Excel and tidy the columns
Store the file on SharePoint with a short note
drudgery: Re-downloading the same CBS tables each month
Retyping agency rate cards from PDFs
Fixing region and job title codes that do not match
today.time_sinks: Finding the right table and reconciling three agency formats takes most of the time; the reading itself is short.

lenses.faster: A scheduled job pulls CBS and UWV tables and agency exports; a model extracts rates from PDF rate cards, so the copy-paste steps disappear.
lenses.autonomous: Each month or when a CAO wage table changes, the refresh runs and posts a one-page summary with source links to the HR Teams channel.
lenses.ambitious: A standing regional labour market file per site, refreshed monthly, that recruiters and the HR Director use when setting pay and planning flex capacity.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses reformatting agency PDFs; what is left is deciding which signals matter for Venlo peak season.
lenses.options: The summary can be cut three ways on request: by site, by job family (order picker, driver, forklift), or by agency.
lenses.altitude: The analyst maintains the source list, the extraction rules and the checks, and reviews the monthly output instead of collecting it.
reach: Recruiter: regional pay and vacancy benchmarks for job ads
FP&A Analyst: flex worker cost inputs for the forecast

tasks.human_edge: Knowing which sources are reliable for Dutch logistics, and noticing when a figure looks wrong for a site the analyst knows.
tasks.pattern_why: Source pulls are deterministic; reading PDF rate cards and report text into fixed fields is an unstructured-to-structured step with checkable output.

in_practice.trigger: Monthly schedule, or a new CAO wage table published
steps: Scheduled script pulls CBS StatLine and UWV tables via their open data endpoints
Model extracts rates and terms from agency rate cards and CAO texts into a fixed Excel template
Rule checks flag missing regions, jumps above a set threshold and unparsed fields
Analyst reviews flags and approves the monthly file
Summary with source links posted to HR Teams channel
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst approves the monthly file before it is shared.
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint folder with source file, extraction output and review note per month

evidence.claim: LLMs can extract fields from PDF rate cards and reports into a fixed schema, with errors that need checking
CBS StatLine publishes open data tables that can be pulled by script

risks: Agency rate cards may be commercially confidential; keep them out of external tools without a data processing agreement
Wrong extraction of a rate that then feeds pay decisions
Source tables change structure and the pull breaks silently
research_questions: Do the three agency portals offer exports or APIs, or only PDFs?
How often does HR actually use this file in a decision today?
Does extraction accuracy on a sample of 20 rate cards reach a level the analyst trusts?

tasks.short: Tell HR and managers what changed in dashboards, reports and definitions, and how to use them.

today.trigger: A new Power BI release, a changed measure, or repeated questions from managers.
steps: Note what changed in the Power BI report or semantic model
Write a Teams post or email to HRBPs and managers
Update the how-to page on SharePoint
Answer follow-up questions one by one
drudgery: Writing the same explanation for several audiences
Answering the same question in chat after the post
Keeping the SharePoint page in step with the report
today.time_sinks: Follow-up questions from managers who did not read the post take more time than the post itself.

lenses.faster: A model drafts release notes from the semantic model change log and report diff, in Dutch and English, in a minute.
lenses.autonomous: On each published change, a draft note is prepared for the analyst to approve and post; the glossary page updates with the same text.
lenses.ambitious: Every manager at all three sites knows what verzuim rate and 90-day retention mean and where to find them, for the first time.
lenses.joy: No more retyping the same note three times; the analyst keeps the part of explaining a number to a team leader who cares.
lenses.options: Three versions per change: a two-line Teams post for team leaders, a detailed note for HRBPs, a technical note for the change log.
lenses.altitude: The analyst owns the glossary and the change log as the single source, and the notes are generated from it.
reach: HR Business Partner: short briefings for site managers
L&D Specialist: short how-to material in Studytube on reading the HR dashboards

tasks.human_edge: Judging what a change means for a site manager and when a change needs a conversation rather than a post.
tasks.pattern_why: Structured change log in, a draft note out, checked against the change log before posting.

in_practice.trigger: Power BI report or semantic model change is published
steps: Change log entry and measure diff are collected from the deployment
Model drafts release notes per audience and updates the glossary text
Analyst checks the draft against the change log and edits
Approved note posted to Teams and SharePoint glossary updated
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst approves each note before posting.
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint change log page with posted note and date

evidence.claim: Copilot in Power BI can summarise reports on Fabric F2+ or Premium capacity; non-English chat is not officially supported
evidence.source: Microsoft Learn, Copilot in Power BI introduction [S5]

evidence.claim: Drafting release notes from a change log is a routine LLM drafting task

risks: A note that misstates a definition spreads the error to every manager
Dutch output quality in Copilot not officially supported
Notes posted unread; dissemination does not change behaviour
research_questions: Does Noordhaven have Fabric or Premium capacity for Copilot in Power BI?
How many manager questions per month repeat something already posted?
Do team leaders on shifts read Teams posts, or is another channel needed?

tasks.short: Write specs for new HR dashboards and reports: fields, definitions, filters, access rules.

today.trigger: An HRBP, the HR Director or finance asks for a new report or a change.
steps: Meet the requester to understand the question
Check which AFAS fields hold the data
Write a spec in Word with measures, filters and row-level security
Get sign-off by mail and file it on SharePoint
drudgery: Writing the same boilerplate sections each time
Looking up AFAS field names and codes
Chasing sign-off
today.time_sinks: Clarifying what the requester actually needs and mapping it to AFAS fields.

lenses.faster: A copilot turns meeting notes into a spec draft using the template and the AFAS field dictionary, and proposes DAX for each measure.
lenses.autonomous: Little runs alone; a request form in Teams pre-fills the spec skeleton when a request arrives.
lenses.ambitious: Every HR measure has a written spec and owner, so the 90-day retention and verzuim numbers mean the same at every site.
lenses.joy: Boilerplate and field lookups go; the analyst keeps the conversation that finds the real question.
lenses.options: For each request, two or three report designs with different scope and effort, so the requester chooses.
lenses.altitude: The analyst curates the spec template, the field dictionary and the definition register that the copilot draws on.
reach: HR Administrator: field-level documentation of AFAS entry rules
Controller: shared definitions for headcount and FTE with finance

tasks.human_edge: Pinning down what a manager means, deciding privacy and access rules, and saying no to a report that should not exist.
tasks.pattern_why: The analyst leads the requirement talk and the decisions; AI speeds drafting and lookups.

in_practice.trigger: Report request submitted through the Teams form
steps: Form fills spec skeleton with requester, purpose and deadline
After the intake meeting, copilot drafts the spec from notes, template and AFAS field dictionary
Analyst edits, sets access rules and minimum group size
Requester signs off in Teams; spec filed on SharePoint
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst writes the final spec; requester signs off; personal data or monitoring capability goes to the works council check.
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint spec library with version history

evidence.claim: Copilot in Power BI writes DAX and works best on a prepared semantic model
Reports on personal data or that can observe performance may need works council consent under WOR 27(1)(k),(l)

risks: Spec drafts that sound complete but miss an access rule
Field dictionary out of date, so the draft maps to wrong AFAS fields
Specs skip the works council check for monitoring-capable reports
research_questions: Is there an AFAS field dictionary today, or must it be built first?
How many report requests per quarter, and how long does a spec take now?
Which past reports would have needed works council consent?

tasks.short: Turn HR trends and outside data into a short recommendation for the HR Director or management.

today.trigger: Quarterly management review, a rise in verzuim or early leavers, or a director's question.
steps: Pull the relevant Power BI figures and outside sources
Compare sites and periods in Excel
Write a memo or PowerPoint with findings and options
Discuss with the HR Director and adjust
drudgery: Rebuilding the same charts for slides
Summarising long external reports
Reformatting for different audiences
today.time_sinks: Assembling figures and reading external reports; the thinking about what to recommend is a smaller part.

lenses.faster: A model summarises external reports with sources and caveats and drafts the memo skeleton from Power BI figures; charts come from the report.
lenses.autonomous: A quarterly draft pack is produced automatically from the dashboards for the analyst to rework.
lenses.ambitious: Each quarter, a short evidence-based note per value stream (hire to productive, absence to return) with a tracked recommendation and its outcome.
lenses.joy: Slide rebuilding goes; the analyst spends time on the argument and the talk with the HR Director.
lenses.options: Three options per issue with cost, effect on 90-day retention or verzuim, and what would show it worked.
lenses.altitude: The analyst sets the question list and evidence standards and checks AI drafts rather than writing each memo from scratch.
reach: HR Business Partner: site-level issue briefs
FP&A Analyst: people cost scenarios

tasks.human_edge: Judging causation, reading the politics, and standing behind a recommendation in front of the HR Director and works council.
tasks.pattern_why: Recommendations carry judgment and accountability; AI drafts and summarises, the analyst decides.

in_practice.trigger: Quarterly review or a threshold breach on a North Star input
steps: Copilot pulls figures from the Power BI semantic model and summarises selected external sources with citations
Analyst checks figures, removes unsupported causal claims
Copilot drafts options with stated assumptions
Analyst finalises and presents to HR Director
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst owns every claim and recommendation.
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint recommendations log with sources and later outcome

evidence.claim: Faster access to information does not by itself lead to better decisions
Trend reports often cannot attribute cause; Workday's own report says its data does not establish how much of the decline AI caused

risks: Plausible but unsupported causal claims in drafts
Absence analysis drifting into causes, which is health data under GDPR Art. 9
Recommendations accepted because they look polished
research_questions: Which recent recommendations were acted on, and what happened?
Do directors want more memos, or fewer and better ones?
Can the semantic model answer the quarterly questions without manual Excel work?

tasks.short: Test that dashboards and reports show correct numbers and answer what the requester asked.

today.trigger: New report release, AFAS change, or a manager saying a number looks wrong.
steps: Reconcile headcount and FTE in Power BI against an AFAS list
Spot-check verzuim and turnover figures by site
Walk the requester through the report for acceptance
Fix and retest
drudgery: Manual reconciliations in Excel each release
Rechecking the same figures after every nightly refresh issue
Tracking test results by mail
today.time_sinks: Manual reconciliation and finding the cause of a mismatch.

lenses.faster: Reconciliation tests run as code after every refresh; the analyst only looks at failures.
lenses.autonomous: Each nightly AFAS extract triggers checks on headcount, FTE, absence days and payroll totals; failures alert the analyst before managers open the dashboard.
lenses.ambitious: A full test suite on every measure, so the analyst can say with evidence that the 90-day retention figure is right.
lenses.joy: No more Excel tie-outs; what remains is the puzzle of a real mismatch.
lenses.options: Test results per site and measure, with a suggested cause ranking for each failure.
lenses.altitude: The analyst designs the test suite and acceptance criteria instead of running checks by hand.
reach: Payroll Specialist: headcount and payroll total tie-out at month close
Controller: HR cost figures reconciled to the general ledger

tasks.human_edge: Deciding whether a report meets the requester's need, and explaining a mismatch to the person who reported it.
tasks.pattern_why: Reconciliation rules can be written down and the output is pass or fail.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly AFAS extract and Power BI refresh
steps: Test script compares Power BI measures with AFAS control totals
Failures and thresholds breached are logged and sent to the analyst in Teams
Model drafts a likely-cause note from the failing rows
Analyst fixes or routes to HR Administrator; acceptance with requester for new reports
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst handles failures and signs off new reports with the requester.
in_practice.logs_to: Test run log table with date, check, result and resolution

evidence.claim: Automated data tests on refreshes are standard BI practice and can be built quickly with AI coding
Text-to-SQL tools still hallucinate tables and columns, so AI-written tests need review

risks: Tests that pass but check the wrong thing
Alert fatigue if thresholds are too tight
Test logs holding personal data kept longer than needed
research_questions: How often did a wrong number reach managers in the last year?
Can AFAS control totals be exported automatically each night?
Which ten checks would have caught the past errors?

tasks.short: Compare how other logistics employers in our regions pay and recruit, and what it means for us.

today.trigger: Hard-to-fill vacancies, low offer acceptance, or pay round preparation.
steps: Collect job ads and pay information of competing warehouses and carriers near each site
Compare with Noordhaven pay, shifts and benefits in Excel
Read agency feedback and exit reasons from Recruitee
Write a short comparison for HR Director and recruiters
drudgery: Reading and coding many job ads by hand
Normalising pay to hourly rates and shift allowances
Repeating the scan each season
today.time_sinks: Manually coding competitor job ads and normalising pay.

lenses.faster: A model codes public job ads into pay, shifts and benefits fields and normalises hourly pay; the analyst checks a sample.
lenses.autonomous: Before peak season and pay rounds, a refreshed comparison is drafted from the latest ads and Recruitee decline reasons.
lenses.ambitious: A per-site employer comparison that explains offer declines and early leavers, used in every pay and recruitment decision.
lenses.joy: Ad coding goes; the analyst keeps the interpretation and the talk with recruiters.
lenses.options: Scenarios: match pay, add a shift allowance, or change schedules, each with cost and expected effect on acceptance.
lenses.altitude: The analyst defines the comparison frame and quality checks; the scan runs as a repeatable job.
reach: Compensation and Benefits Specialist: market pay benchmarks
Recruiter: employer value messaging per site

tasks.human_edge: Knowing the local labour market and what a driver or picker in Venlo actually weighs, and turning it into a defensible choice.
tasks.pattern_why: Data coding is automatable, but the strategic reading and pay advice stay with the analyst.

in_practice.trigger: Season planning, pay round, or offer acceptance below target
steps: Collect public job ads for target roles per site
Model codes ads into a fixed schema; analyst checks a sample
Combine with Recruitee decline reasons and agency data
Copilot drafts scenarios; analyst finalises advice
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst reviews coding sample and owns the advice.
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint folder with coded data, sample check and advice

evidence.claim: LLMs can code job ad text into structured pay and benefit fields

risks: Scraping job sites may breach their terms
Advertised pay differs from paid pay
Sharing pay data with competitors or via agencies could raise competition-law concerns
research_questions: Is offer acceptance actually lost to pay, or to shifts and travel?
Which public sources give enough regional job ads legally?
Would the Compensation and Benefits Specialist use this, or buy a benchmark?

tasks.short: Produce required HR reports: verzuim, headcount, turnover, works council and CBS figures.

today.trigger: Monthly close, quarterly works council meeting, annual social report, or a CBS survey request.
steps: Run AFAS extracts and refresh Power BI
Copy figures into Excel and Word templates
Write explanatory text on changes
Check with Payroll and HR Director, then send
drudgery: Copying figures into templates
Rewriting the same explanation each period
Fixing late AFAS corrections
today.time_sinks: Assembly and last-minute corrections after AFAS data changes.

lenses.faster: Reports fill from the semantic model on schedule; a model drafts the narrative on what changed and why the figures moved.
lenses.autonomous: Monthly verzuim and headcount reports run and send by subscription after data checks pass; required filings wait for approval.
lenses.ambitious: Verzuim and 90-day retention correct by day 2 of each month at all sites, with the works council getting the same numbers as management.
lenses.joy: Template copying goes; what remains is explaining trends and answering the works council.
lenses.options: Narrative drafts at three depths: one line for site managers, a paragraph for HR Director, a full note for the works council.
lenses.altitude: The analyst owns definitions, checks and report schedules; the reports produce themselves.
reach: HR Administrator: monthly absence list checks
Payroll Specialist: headcount figures for payroll close
Controller: FTE and people cost figures for month-end

tasks.human_edge: Signing off figures that go to the works council or authorities, and explaining sensitive changes.
tasks.pattern_why: Figures come from fixed definitions on structured AFAS data; an llm_step adds the narrative.

steps: Data quality checks run on AFAS extract
Power BI paginated reports generate on schedule
Model drafts change narrative from period comparison
Routine reports send by subscription; required filings go to analyst for approval
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst approves works council, social report and CBS submissions.
in_practice.logs_to: Report run log with version sent and approver

evidence.claim: Absence data is health data; the Dutch DPA fined a company partly for recording sick leave causes
evidence.source: GDPR Art. 9 [S13]; AWVN on AP fine [S14]

evidence.claim: Power BI subscriptions and scheduled refresh deliver standard reports

risks: Reports showing absence causes or small groups that identify people
Sending figures before late AFAS corrections
Narrative stating causes the data cannot show
research_questions: Which reports are legally or contractually required, and to whom?
How often are figures corrected after sending?
What minimum group size does the works council accept?

tasks.short: Keep the SharePoint library of report templates, definitions, DAX snippets and specs up to date.

today.trigger: New report, changed definition, or someone cannot find a template.
steps: Save new templates and specs to SharePoint
Update the definition register by hand
Remove or mark outdated versions
Point colleagues to the right file
drudgery: Tagging and naming files
Finding duplicates and old versions
Answering where-is-it questions
today.time_sinks: Cleaning duplicates and keeping definitions in sync with the semantic model.

lenses.faster: A script compares semantic model measures with the definition register; a model tags new files and flags duplicates.
lenses.autonomous: Each published change updates the register entry and flags templates using an old definition.
lenses.ambitious: A complete, searchable metric and template library that managers and agents use as the source for every HR answer.
lenses.joy: Filing and deduplication go; the analyst keeps designing good templates.
lenses.options: For each duplicate cluster, a proposed merge with the differences shown.
lenses.altitude: The library becomes the metric layer the analyst owns: definitions, verified answers and access rules.
reach: HR Administrator: template upkeep for HR letters
Controller: shared FTE and headcount definitions

tasks.human_edge: Deciding which definition is the official one and keeping finance and HR aligned.
tasks.pattern_why: Sync and duplicate checks are rule-based; an llm_step tags and summarises.

in_practice.trigger: Semantic model publish or new file in the library
steps: Script compares model measures with register
Model tags new files and flags near-duplicates
Analyst approves merges and definition changes
Register and library update
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst approves any definition change or merge.
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint version history and register change log

evidence.claim: Copilot in Power BI misinterprets data without a prepared semantic model, so a maintained metric layer matters

risks: Auto-tagging spreads wrong labels
Old templates still in use outside the library
Library sprawl without an owner
research_questions: How many templates and definitions exist and how many are duplicates?
Can semantic model metadata be read by script in Noordhaven's Power BI tenant?
Who in finance co-owns shared definitions?

role.altitude: From producing reports and memos to owning Noordhaven's HR metric layer: definitions, tests, verified answers, access rules and works council approved uses that managers, dashboards and agents draw on.
reach: HR Administrator: AFAS data quality checks and correction lists
Payroll Specialist: headcount and payroll tie-outs at month close
Compensation and Benefits Specialist: regional pay benchmarks
Recruiter: pipeline and offer acceptance analysis
FP&A Analyst: flex worker and people cost inputs
Controller: shared FTE and headcount definitions
role.ceiling_note: About 40 to 55% of the time on these tasks can be freed, mostly in collecting, copying and checking. Limits: data quality in AFAS, Power BI capacity for Copilot, works council consent for anything able to observe performance, GDPR limits on absence data, and the judgment and trust needed for recommendations. Individual risk scores stay out.
skills_to_grow: Semantic model design and governance in Power BI
Automated data testing in Python or Power Automate
Prompt and evaluation design for LLM steps
GDPR, WOR and EU AI Act knowledge for HR analytics
Writing clear recommendations for the HR Director and works council
role.ambitious_version: One analyst runs a self-checking HR data service: North Star inputs (90-day retention, verzuim, time to hire) correct by day 2 at all three sites, managers getting answers from a gated assistant on a prepared model, quarterly evidence-based recommendations tracked to outcome, and a regional labour market view used in every pay and flex decision, all agreed with the works council.
